Because CCPP is caused by Mycoplasma capricolum subsp. capripneumoniae and responds to macrolide/tetracycline antibiotics, Contagious Caprine Pleuropneumonia is the most likely diagnosis over Peste des Petits Ruminants, Pasteurellosis, Verminous pneumonia and Caseous lymphadenitis. Recommended: Tylosin 10.0 mg/kg IM with supportive nursing. Fever measured 41.0 C.

Microscopy confirmed haemonchus contortus (parasitaemia 3.7%). No culture & sensitivity report was available for this case. Recommended: Albendazole 7.5 mg/kg PO with supportive nursing. Fever measured 39.6 C.

clinician_rationale: A 24-month-old Sahiwal bovine presented with pyrexia, lymphadenopathy, dyspnoea, nasal discharge and inappetence (temperature 41.6 C). Microscopy confirmed theileria parva (parasitaemia 1.5%). No culture & sensitivity report was available for this case. Clinically, prescapular/parotid lymph-node enlargement with Theileria parva schizonts on lymph-node smear is characteristic of East Coast Fever. East-African context and differentials (Trypanosomiasis, Anaplasmosis and Babesiosis) were considered before settling on East Coast Fever. Recommended management is Buparvaquone 2.5 mg/kg IM with supportive care.
